Madurai.overview: Madurai, known as the Temple City, is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
Madurai.special: Called Athens of the East, famous for temples, arts, and festivals like Chithirai Thiruvizha.
Madurai.food: Famous for Jigarthanda, Kari dosa, Paruthi paal (cottonseed milk).
Madurai.culture: Strong Tamil culture with ancient Sangam literature influence.

Chennai.overview: Chennai, the capital of Tamil Nadu, is a cultural, economic, and educational hub of South India.
Chennai.special: Known as the 'Gateway to South India', famous for Bharatanatyam dance and Carnatic music.
Chennai.food: Famous for Filter Coffee, Idli-Sambar, and Chettinad Cuisine.
Chennai.culture: Blend of traditional Tamil culture and modern cosmopolitan lifestyle.

Coimbatore.overview: Coimbatore, also called the Manchester of South India, is a major industrial city in Tamil Nadu.
Coimbatore.special: Renowned for textile industries, Kovai Cora cotton, and educational institutions.
Coimbatore.food: Famous for Murukku, Halwa, and unique Kongu Nadu cuisine.
Coimbatore.culture: Mix of Kongu traditions with modern industrial culture.

Trichy.overview: Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) is a historical city in Tamil Nadu located on the banks of river Cauvery.
Trichy.special: Known as Rockfort City, famous for ancient temples and educational institutions like NIT Trichy.
Trichy.food: Famous for Jigarthanda, Puliyodarai (tamarind rice), and traditional Tamil meals.
Trichy.culture: Rich in temple architecture and Tamil religious traditions.
